name: Industrial CCTV-HH Dataset
description: Hard-hat compliance detection is a key component of vision-based industrial safety monitoring. Public hard-hat datasets support model development but rarely reflect real industrial closed-circuit television (CCTV) conditions, such as fixed elevated viewpoints, small object scale, temporal correlation between frames, partial occlusion, and privacy-sensitive content. We address three questions: whether public datasets generalize to industrial CCTV, why temporal separation matters for video-derived data, and whether privacy-preserving preprocessing degrades detection. We introduce the Industrial CCTV-HH Dataset, an AI-ready, privacy-preserving object detection resource built from real surveillance recordings in an operational industrial facility, containing 2413 images and 9608 annotated head-region instances in two classes (head without helmet, head with helmet). A day-level temporal split reduces near-duplicate leakage and yields deployment-oriented evaluation. A preprocessing pipeline uses a generative image-inpainting model (LaMa) to remove on-screen overlays and textual identifiers and adds localized face anonymization while preserving head structure, illustrating generative image editing for privacy-preserving dataset preparation.
